claim: Sacro Monte di Orta is a UNESCO World Heritage site with 20 chapels on Saint Francis's life; chapels open 9:30-18:00 weekdays and 9:30-18:30 weekends/holidays from 29 March to 24 October 2026; free admission; about a 20-minute walk from Orta on a sloped paved cobbled road with steps.
quote: Monday to Friday from 9:30am. to 6:00pm; Saturday, Sunday and public holidays from 9:30am to 6:30pm

claim: The public Navigazione Orta boat service from Orta to Isola San Giulio runs every 15 minutes starting 9:00 a.m. daily, with a €5.00 return fare.
quote: €5,00* return ... Every 15 minutes ... starting at 9.00 a.m.

claim: Private motoscafi consortium boats cost about €5 round-trip and start earlier and run more frequently than the public ferry (€3.80 round-trip, every 30-45 minutes); crossing takes about 5 minutes.
quote: Motorboats cost €5 round-trip and start earlier and run more frequently ... Public ferries cost €3.80 round-trip ... every 30 to 45 minutes

claim: The Basilica di San Giulio dates to the 4th century (current 12th-century Romanesque structure built on a 5th-century church), with frescoes of the Apostles from the 14th-16th centuries and a four-pillared black marble pulpit with animal carvings as old as the church; San Giulio's remains lie in the crypt.
quote: The current 12th-century Romanesque structure was built on top of an older church from the 5th century ... frescoes depicting the Apostles ... between the 14th and 16th centuries

claim: Palazzotto della Comunità on Piazza Motta was built in 1582 and served as the meeting place for the General Council of the Republic of the Riviera d'Orta from 1345-1753; the Basilica frescoes include baroque works by Carlo Borsetti and Francesco del Cairo; Sacro Monte is about 24 minutes' walk from the main square.
quote: 1582 palace sits on Piazza Motta's left side and formerly served as the meeting place for the small Republic of the Riviera d'Orta's general council (1345-1753)

claim: Villa Crespi is the trailhead for walking routes that pass through Piazza Motta and connect to the surrounding lake panoramic trails.
quote: starts from Orta San Giulio, in particular from Piazza Motta ... At Villa Crespi you'll come to Crociera

claim: Sacro Monte di Orta sits on a hilltop overlooking the lake and Isola San Giulio; visitors should allow 1.5-2 hours and wear comfortable shoes.
quote: Admission is free, and you should allow 1.5-2 hours for your visit; comfortable shoes are highly recommended

claim: The Mater Ecclesiae Benedictine abbey on Isola San Giulio was founded in 1973 as a cloistered community of nuns dedicated to the Marian feast of Mary, Mater Ecclesiae; the nuns produce liturgical paraments.
quote: It was founded in 1973. It is dedicated to the Marian Patronal Feast of Mary, Mater Ecclesiae. The nuns are known for the production of paraments.

claim: Villa Crespi is roughly a 10-12 minute walk from Piazza Motta in Orta San Giulio; the historic centre is entirely pedestrianised with the Wednesday market on Piazza Motta dating to 1228.
quote: the quaint town of Orta San Giulio can be easily reached on foot from Villa Crespi with a beautiful 10-minute walk ... Since 1228, the market has been held here on Wednesdays

claim: Sacro Monte di Orta is roughly 600 metres from Villa Crespi and can be reached from the end of the Sacro Monte route down the other side of the hill to Villa Crespi in about 15 minutes.
quote: Just 600 meters from Villa Crespi ... from the end of the Sacro Monte course, you can descend on the other side of the hill and get to Villa Crespi in about 15 minutes

claim: The Way of Silence (Via del Silenzio) is a cobblestoned alleyway encircling the island lined with multilingual signs in four languages inviting silent reflection, taking around 10-30 minutes depending on pace.
quote: cobble-stoned alleyway that circles the island ... signs written in 4 languages with sayings to encourage reflection

claim: Stresa to Villa Crespi in Orta San Giulio is roughly 14 miles (~22 km) and about 23 minutes by car.
quote: The driving distance between Stresa to Relais & Chateaux Villa Crespi, Orta San Giulio is 14 miles. It takes approximately 23 minutes to drive from Stresa to Relais & Chateaux Villa Crespi, Orta San Giulio.

claim: Isola Bella's Palazzo Borromeo opens for the 2026 season from 12 March to 8 November, with adult tickets at €25 plus a €0.50 landing fee.
quote: Isola Bella is open from March 12 to November 8, 2026... Adults pay €25, while children (6-15 years) pay €16. There is also a €0.50 landing fee per person payable on the spot.

claim: Navigazione Laghi runs Lake Maggiore ferries on the summer timetable from 29 March to 4 October 2026, with departures roughly every 30 minutes in the Borromean bay from around 08:00 to 18:00.
quote: The summer timetable for Lake Maggiore valid from 29th March to 4th October 2026 is currently in effect.

claim: Isola Madre's 8-hectare botanical gardens are among Italy's oldest, laid out in English style in the late 18th century, with a famed Piazzale dei Pappagalli featuring free-roaming parrots, peacocks and pheasants.
quote: One of the oldest botanical gardens in Italy, the present English garden-style park was landscaped in the early 19th century... Piazzale dei Pappagalli - parrots, peacocks, pheasants, etc.

claim: Isola dei Pescatori is the only permanently inhabited Borromean island, a small fishermen's village (~100x350 m) packed with seafood trattorias and balconied houses once used for drying fish.
quote: The island's old town is a walkable warren with heaps of fairytale appeal, historic architecture, crisscrossing alleyways, and a surprisingly large collection of restaurants serving fresh seafood and hearty Piedmont cuisine paired with mountain views.

claim: The Consorzio Motoscafisti Isole Borromee runs smaller private motorboats (37 seats, partly open) alongside the public Navigazione Laghi service for island hopping from Stresa.
quote: Modern boats with all mod cons, microphone, and music diffusion that are partially open for sunny days and completely covered in case of rain, with each boat carrying 37 seated people plus the crew.

claim: Navigazione Laghi public ferries are the cheaper, schedule-reliable option with easier boarding via ramps, while the private motoscafisti board from a narrower pier slightly north.
quote: The Municipal Ferry operates larger, white ferry boats with 132 person capacity that dock using loading ramps at the main and island piers, and run on published ferry schedules with cheap, prompt, and efficient hop-on, hop-off service.

claim: Stresa's Corso Umberto I lakefront promenade is lined with Belle Époque grand hotels and villas with Alp views across the lake.
quote: The lungolago—the lakefront promenade that stretches endlessly along the water's edge features grand dames of architecture, all Belle Époque façades and wrought iron balconies.

claim: The Grand Hotel des Iles Borromées, open since 1863 with a preserved Belle Époque interior, is the most iconic of Stresa's historic lakefront hotels.
quote: The most prominent hotel is the Grand Hotel des Iles Borromées, which has been the place to stay since 1863, featuring a Belle Époque façade with salons and rooms that preserve the shimmering chandeliers, rich fabrics and timeless elegance of a bygone era.

claim: A combined Isola Bella + Isola Madre ticket is around €36.50 in 2026, separate from the Navigazione Laghi day ferry pass which costs about €16.90.
quote: The combined ticket for Isola Madre + Isola Bella costs €36.50... The ferry day ticket costs €16.90 for adults.

claim: The Stresa–Alpino–Mottarone cable car from Piazzale Lido in Carciano has remained closed since the fatal 23 May 2021 accident, with no confirmed reopening for 2026.
quote: The aerial tramway has remained closed ever since the Stresa-Mottarone cable car disaster on 23 May 2021.

claim: From Monday 4 May 2026 the Lake Maggiore timetable adds services 142 and 143 on the Stresa–Islands–Baveno route, while Campione stops are suspended from 16 May 2026.
quote: With effect from Monday 4 May, the timetable will be updated to include services 142 and 143 on the Stresa – Islands – Baveno and Baveno – Stresa routes... All stops to Campione are suspended from 16th May 2026.

claim: Stresa's official tourism office confirms the cablecar remains closed with no announced reopening; tourist office hours run through November 2026.
quote: THE CABLECAR IS CLOSED

claim: The cable car operator and engineers admitted to blocking emergency brakes to avoid downtime, which became routine practice prior to the disaster.
quote: blocking the emergency brakes had become common practice to avoid downtime when brakes were malfunctioning

claim: Alpyland alpine coaster operates 10:00-17:00 weekdays and 10:00-18:00 weekends; single full ride €6.50, single reduced ride €5.50, with multi-ride packages up to 10 trips.
quote: Single trip: €6.50 | 2 trips: €13.00 | 3 trips: €19.50 | 4 trips: €22.00

claim: Alpyland requires riders to be at least 4 years old and 100 cm tall; the two-seat bobsleds have rider-adjustable speed.
quote: All children aged 4 and above, with a minimum height of 100 cm, can ride

claim: Giardino Botanico Alpinia is open daily 9:30-18:00 weather permitting, with full admission €5.00 and reduced €4.50 for children 4-12 or groups.
quote: dalle 9.30 alle 18.00 TUTTI I GIORNI, FESTIVI INCLUSI

claim: Giardino Botanico Alpinia sits at roughly 800 m altitude above Stresa and specializes in alpine flora.
quote: alpine plants, located at 800 meters altitude above Stresa on Lake Maggiore

claim: From Mottarone's 1,491 m summit, seven lakes are visible: Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Comabbio, Monate, Varese and Biandronno.
quote: From Mottarone's top you can see 7 different lakes: Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Comabbio, Monate, Varese and Biandronno

claim: The Parco del Mottarone summit (1,492 m) offers a 360° panorama and over 15 km of ski slopes in winter, plus the Rifugio Genziana refuge restaurant.
quote: seven shimmering lakes: Maggiore, Orta, Mergozzo, Varese, Comabbio, Monate, and Biandronno

claim: The summit panorama spans from the Ligurian Apennines and Maritime Alps to Monte Rosa, Monviso, and the Swiss high peaks across the Po Plain.
quote: uninterrupted 360° panorama from the Ligurian Apennines and the Maritime Alps to the Monte Rosa massif, the Monviso and the high peaks of Switzerland

claim: The Mottarone MTB area has an extensive trail network with maintained singletrack across difficulty grades; the Mottarone Trail Park has about ten routes starting from Bar Stazione near Alpino with on-site bike rental.
quote: Mottarone Trail Park offers about ten maintained single-track routes of varying difficulty, all starting and ending at the Bar Stazione near Alpino

claim: Mottarone is accessible by road from Armeno on the Lake Orta side (the 'Due Riviere') or by the private Borromea toll road from Stresa-Gignese.
quote: the 'Due Riviere' road from Armeno, or the private 'Borromea' road (toll) from Stresa-Gignese

claim: The Borromea private toll road from Alpino costs €10 for cars and €7 for motorbikes, while the Armeno road from Lake Orta is free of charge.
quote: The fee for the private Borromea toll road is €10 for cars and €7 for motorbikes

claim: Villa Crespi's own magazine highlights Mottarone for its seven-lake panorama, hiking through pine-fir-beech-larch-chestnut forests, and winter ski runs.
quote: the natural splendor of the 'Seven Lakes'... Orta, Maggiore, Mergozzo, Biandronno, Varese, Monate, and Comabbio

claim: Mottarone is roughly a half-hour winding drive from Orta via Armeno, with the route considered the natural mountain backdrop to Lake Orta.
quote: Mottarone is one of the lowest peaks of all the Alps, but reserves to the visitors one of the most beautiful landescape

claim: Villa Taranto 2026 ticket prices: Adults €15, Youth 12-26 €10, Children 6-11 €2.50; full daily operation March 19-September 20, 9 AM-6:30 PM
quote: Adults: €15.00, Children (12-26 years): €10.00, Children (6-11 years): €2.50 ... March 19-September 20: Daily operations, 9 AM-6:30 PM

claim: Villa Taranto 2026 season opens earlier than usual on March 6 and runs through November 1, with full daily hours from March 19
quote: Starting from March 6, 2026, earlier than in previous years ... Full Hours (March 19 onward): Daily operations begin with regular scheduling

claim: Villa Taranto's Bulb Festival (tulips) is scheduled 22 March - 20 April, and the Dahlia Display runs from July to late October, meaning late May falls between these signature displays
quote: Bulb Festival: Scheduled: 22 March - 20 April ... Dahlia Display: Scheduled: from July to late October

claim: Villa Taranto's Rhododendron Wood holds about 800 specimens, a major May attraction along sloping terrain
quote: Rhododendron Wood extends along the sloping part of the Garden ... approximately 800 specimens of rhododendron species and cultivars

claim: At Villa Taranto, rhododendrons, azaleas, camellias and exotic plants bloom from May into summer; water lilies unfurl in pools from late spring
quote: Rhododendrons, azaleas, camellias and countless exotic plants bloom from May into the summer ... water lilies unfurl their colorful flowers in tranquil pools

claim: Parco Pallavicino 2026: open March 12 - October 24 daily 10 AM-5 PM last entry; single adult ticket €18, ages 6-15 €13, ages 3-5 €5; closed May 22, 2026 for Giro d'Italia
quote: March 12 – October 24: Daily from 10:00 a.m. to 05:00 p.m. (last entrance) ... Adult: €18.00, Ages 6-15: €13.00 ... The park will close on May 22, 2026 due to the Giro d'Italia

claim: Combined Borromean tickets 2026: Isola Bella + Parco Pallavicino €37 adult; three-site pass (any 3 of Isola Bella/Madre/Pallavicino/Angera) €55 adult, valid two consecutive days
quote: Isola Bella + Parco Pallavicino: €37.00 for adults ... 3 locations: €55.00 for adults ... valid for two consecutive days

claim: Parco Pallavicino is an 18-hectare park combining historic gardens with a zoological area featuring deer, llamas, alpacas, peacocks, kangaroos and 40+ animal species, plus roses, azaleas, rhododendrons
quote: more than 18 hectares of green space ... deer, Tibetan goats, llamas, peacocks, alpacas, and kangaroos ... lawns, shady avenues and open spaces planted with roses, oleanders, magnolias, daffodils, azaleas, and rhododendrons

claim: Villa San Remigio is currently closed to the public, with garden landscaping and significant renovation underway in anticipation of a future reopening
quote: The garden is being upgraded with landscaping and a significant renovation in anticipation of an upcoming opening to the public

claim: Villa San Remigio's main villa was acquired by the Italian State in the 1960s and remains inaccessible, used only for bureaucratic offices; only the waterfront chapel portion is private rental
quote: was acquired by the Italian State in the 60's and is now inaccessible, hosting only bureaucrat's offices

claim: Orta San Giulio to Verbania-Pallanza is about 14 road miles (~22 km), roughly 23 minutes by car — well within the 30 km radius from Villa Crespi
quote: The distance between Orta San Giulio and Verbania-Pallanza is 11 miles, with a road distance of 14 miles. The driving time takes approximately 23 minutes

claim: The Anello Azzurro (Blue Ring) circumnavigates Lake Orta over three stages totalling about 43.6 km with 1,150 m of elevation gain, rated moderate.
quote: Total Length: 43.6 km ... Number of Stages: 3 days with 3-4 h/day ... Elevation Gain/Loss: 1,150 m each direction ... Difficulty: Moderate

claim: The Blue Ring is marked with blue-ring 'Anello Azzurro' signs and red/white CAI marks, mixing trail, asphalt and dirt road.
quote: The route is mixed (trail, asphalt, dirt road) and is marked with 'Anello Azzurro' blue ring signs and red/white marks

claim: The Sanctuary of Madonna del Sasso stands on a granite cliff above Pella at 338 m, with a panoramic 'balcony of Cusio' overlooking most of Lake Orta.
quote: The Sanctuary of Madonna del Sasso stands on a granite rock rising above the village of Pella and the mirror of Lake Orta at an altitude of 338 meters ... the balcony of Cusio

claim: A signed hike climbs from Pella through Boleto up to the Madonna del Sasso sanctuary above the west shore.
quote: Hike Pella - Boleto - Madonna del Sasso

claim: Canoe Lago d'Orta in Orta San Giulio rents kayaks, SUPs and pedalos at the lakefront near San Giulio Island.
quote: Canoe Lago d'Orta Eco-Water Sports and Leisure Kayak SUP Pedalò Rental

claim: RS Rental in Pettenasco (Via 1° Maggio 1) rents kayaks, SUPs, e-bikes, scooters and cars for Lake Orta excursions.
quote: Noleggio Kayak, SUP, Biciclette Auto e Motorini Lago d'Orta

claim: Freedome offers guided kayak tours on Lake Orta from about €65, with shorter Pettenasco departures from €35 per person.
quote: Canoa e kayak Lago d'Orta | A partire da €65

claim: Lago di Mergozzo is described as one of the cleanest lakes in Italy thanks to its motorboat ban.
quote: one of the cleanest lakes in all of Italy ... No motorboats disturb its waters

claim: Lago di Mergozzo's strict no-motorboat policy and efficient sewage system make its waters among the clearest in Italy, ideal for swimming and SUP.
quote: Due to the absence of industrial activity, a ban on motor boats, and an efficient sewage system, its waters are amongst the clearest in Italy

claim: Lido di Gozzano is the largest beach on Lake Orta (about 150 m), with Europe's highest lake trampoline; open daily except Wednesday, 9:30–18:00.
quote: the largest beach on the lake and is characterized by the highest trampoline in a lake in all of Europe ... 150 meters long

claim: Pettenasco hosts Dolphin's Beach (bar, restaurant, showers) and Approdo (loungers, changing rooms, on-beach swimming pool); Pella's beach is in the Roncallo hamlet, reachable by car (14 km via SP229) or boat.
quote: Dolphin's Beach ... bar, restaurant, showers and toilets ... Approdo Beach ... deckchairs and umbrellas, changing rooms, shower, sinks, swimming pool on the beach ... Pella Beach ... Roncallo hamlet

claim: E-Bike Lago d'Orta in Orta San Giulio rents Scott e-bikes for adults, junior bikes for kids 9+, and child seats; open April–September, 9–18.
quote: Scott brand e-bikes ... junior e-bikes for children aged 9 and up ... open from April to September, from 9am to 6pm

claim: CCT Bike Rental delivers e-bikes around Lake Orta from Pettenasco, with delivery to Omegna, Stresa, Verbania, Arona or Ispra (3-day advance booking, 2-day minimum).
quote: Bookings must be submitted at least 3 days in advance with a minimum of 2 bike rental days. Delivery service is available around Lake Orta to places like Omegna, Stresa, Verbania, Arona or Ispra

claim: Lake Orta's average May water temperature is about 15.5 °C (range 11–21 °C) — cool for swimming without a wetsuit.
quote: In May, the average water temperature in Lake Orta is 15.5°C, with a minimum of 11°C and a maximum of 21°C

claim: Lake Orta is promoted as among Europe's cleanest lakes for swimming and watersports, including SUP, kayak and open-water swims.
quote: Sport water activity Lago d'Orta - splash the real nature

claim: The Alessi factory outlet sits at via privata Alessi 6 in Crusinallo di Omegna, open Mon–Sun 10:00–18:00, selling catalogue items plus discounted seconds and end-of-range pieces next to the Alessi factory itself.
quote: The Alessi outlet store is located at 6 privata Alessi street in Crusinallo di Omegna, and is open Monday to Sunday from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

claim: The Museo Alessi, across the driveway from the outlet, requires booking at least two weeks ahead for a guided visit with a team member.
quote: The Museo Alessi is across the driveway from the outlet store, and reservations are required at least two weeks in advance to see the museum with a member of the team.

claim: Forum Omegna occupies the reconverted Cobianchi steelworks site and was designed by Alessandro Mendini, hosting since 1998 a permanent collection of household design from Alessi, Calderoni, Girmi, Lagostina, La Nuova Faro, Irmel, Tracanzan and Piazza.
quote: The reconversion of the area from a place of work and hardship to a new cultural and artistic center was entrusted to the prestigious studio of the architect Mendini... Since 1998, the Forum in Omegna has housed a rich collection of household objects by companies that have made Italian and world history

claim: The Sanctuary of Madonna del Sasso rises on a granite outcrop above Pella at 338 m, completed in 1748 with a Greek-cross Baroque plan, frescoes by Lorenzo Peracino and an altarpiece Pietà by Fermo Stella da Caravaggio.
quote: stands on a granite rock rising above the village of Pella and the mirror of Lake Orta at an altitude of 338 meters... The church has a Greek cross plan in Baroque style... the architecture and frescoes are the work of the Valsesian painter-architect Lorenzo Peracino.

claim: The forecourt of the sanctuary is locally called the 'balcony of Cusio' and offers a panorama spanning the lake, Mottarone, the Alps and the Novara plain.
quote: From the square in front of the church, called "the balcony of Cusio", there is a breathtaking view of almost the entire lake, Mount Mottarone, the Alps, and the plain towards Novara.

claim: San Maurizio d'Opaglio's Museo del Rubinetto e della sua Tecnologia is billed as unique in the world, telling the story of human relationships with water through faucet and valve technology.
quote: Museum of the Faucet and its Technology of San Maurizio d'Opaglio is unique in the world; it addresses the fascinating relationship of humans with water through the history of hygiene and technological innovations

claim: San Maurizio d'Opaglio is known as the 'capital of the faucet'; the museum offers free admission Friday–Sunday 15:00–18:00.
quote: San Maurizio d'Opaglio is known as the "capital of the faucet"... Admission is free, and hours are Friday-Sunday from 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm.

claim: Pettenasco's Museo dell'Arte della Tornitura del Legno occupies a former Maulini family wood-turning workshop that operated 1886–1970, sited in the historic centre near the Medieval House and town hall square.
quote: the museum is located in an old wood turning workshop that belongs to the Maulini family, which operated their business there from 1886 to 1970. The museum is situated in the historic center of Pettenasco a few steps from the Medieval House and Town Hall Square.

claim: Wood turning was the defining Cusio craft, with many workshops producing turned-wood objects in the area until the 1950s, when industrial homeware took over.
quote: Wood turning was a typical type of craftsmanship in the Cusio area, with many businesses producing objects in turned wood until the Fifties.

claim: Cantine Aperte Alto Piemonte 2026 runs 30–31 May with Gattinara DOCG, Ghemme DOCG, Boca, Bramaterra and Colline Novaresi cellars open for visits.
quote: Cantine Aperte Alto Piemonte 2026 will be held on May 30 and 31, with Gattinara DOCG, Ghemme DOCG, Boca, Bramaterra and Colline Novaresi opening their doors.

claim: The Strada del Vino delle Colline Novaresi spans 13 municipalities including Boca, Ghemme, Sizzano, Fara Novarese, Romagnano Sesia, Briona, Suno and Cavaglio d'Agogna.
quote: The Wine Route of the Novarese Hills involves 13 municipalities including Barengo, Boca, Bogogno, Briona, Cavaglio d'Agogna, Cressa, Fara Novarese, Ghemme, Marano Ticino, Mezzomerico, Romagnano Sesia, Sizzano and Suno.

claim: Villa Crespi confirms that Ghemme and Gattinara cellars are about 30 minutes from Lake Orta and offers a wine-tour package with private transfer.
quote: the wine cellars between Ghemme and Gattinara are just 30 minutes away from Lake Orta, and Villa Crespi offers organized wine tours to this area with private transfer.

claim: Tapulone is the culinary symbol of Borgomanero — a slow-cooked stew of minced donkey meat with lard, onion, garlic, red wine, cabbage, bay, cloves and rosemary, served with polenta.
quote: Tapulone is a traditional dish and a culinary symbol of the city of Borgomanero... It's prepared with beaten lard, extra virgin olive oil, onions, garlic, local red wine, minced donkey meat, cabbage, and various herbs and spices such as bay leaves, cloves, and rosemary.

claim: Alfonso Bialetti, born 1888 in Omegna, opened an aluminium semi-finished products workshop there in 1919 and invented the Moka Express in 1933; the 'omino con i baffi' logo was added in 1953 and a state-of-the-art Omegna factory followed in 1956.
quote: Alfonso Bialetti was born in 1888 in Omegna, in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. In 1919 in the village of Omegna, Piedmonte, Alfonso Bialetti opened a workshop for the manufacture of aluminum semi-finished products.

claim: Omegna's homeware lineage — Lagostina, Alessi, Piazza, Bialetti — grew out of the Cane family's pioneering metalworking; Lagostina's 1955 'Thermoplan' double-bottom innovation paired steel and aluminium.
quote: It was Lagostina who once again found a solution in 1955 by using bases made of "Thermoplan"®: a system that involved coupling steel and aluminium in order to create the so-called "double bottom".

claim: Miacce are paper-thin waffle-like discs made since the 15th century in a long-handled iron heated over fire, batter of milk, flour and eggs, served with soft cheese or jam — round in Piedmont, rectangular in Valle d'Aosta.
quote: Miacce are crispy paper-thin treats made since the 15th century in a waffle iron called a notai heated over an open fire, prepared from a batter of milk, flour (wheat or corn) and eggs, and often served with soft cheeses or jam.

claim: Gorgonzola DOP can legally be produced only in a defined set of provinces including Novara and Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, putting the cheese's heartland directly around Lake Orta.
quote: Gorgonzola can only be produced in the provinces of Novara, Bergamo, Brescia, Como, Cremona, Cuneo, Lecco, Lodi, Milan, Pavia, Varese, Verbano-Cusio-Ossola and Vercelli
